title: 'Hauntcheck': How a Micanopy 5th grader turned paranormal investigations into a viral hit
excerpt: Blaine Pool, a 10-year-old in Micanopy, and his dad Cory surpassed 207,000 YouTube subscribers on their paranormal investigation channel 'Hauntcheck.'
content:
MICANOPY, Fla. — What began as a father-son hobby exploring mysterious stories has grown into a YouTube channel with more than 207,000 subscribers — and one of the creators leading the investigations is just 10 years old.

With Halloween approaching, many families are preparing for costumes and trick-or-treating, but Blaine Pool and his father, Cory Pool, spend their time investigating reports of ghosts and unexplained events on their channel, “Hauntcheck.”

Blaine, a fifth grader at Micanopy Area Cooperative School, helped the channel reach a milestone achieved by only about 1.3% of YouTube creators.

From a Fort McCoy investigation to a global audience

Cory and Blaine Pool launched “Hauntcheck” never expecting it to grow beyond family and friends.

“When Blaine started to show an interest in it, he thought, we have the equipment. Why not do it? We just thought it would be our family and friends looking, though we didn’t think that there would be 200 plus thousand,” said Cory Pool, producer for “Hauntcheck.”

Their first video, filmed about a month ago, took them to an old house in Fort McCoy with a history of reported paranormal activity. That investigation helped set the stage for the channel’s rapid growth.

Now, the father-and-son team analyzes footage submitted by viewers around the world, reviewing scenes — including clips like a swing moving on its own — to examine possible explanations.

“I think a lot of things are hidden from us. A lot of things, you know, we just don’t understand,” Cory Pool said. “But that’s the point of our channel is to try to get to the bottom of it and try to separate fact from fiction.”

Support from classmates and teachers

Balancing fifth grade with content creation has been made easier by classmates and teachers in Micanopy who encourage Blaine’s work.

“My friends are, like, really supportive, really happy for me, and like, a lot of the teachers are pretty supportive too. Like, one of our teachers was, like, one of the reasons we got over 20 subscribers,” Blaine Pool said.

For Blaine, the draw comes down to encountering moments that defy easy answers.

“Just getting spooked kind of is fun, so that’s like one of the big reasons that I wanted to start this,” Blaine Pool said. “Okay, I can’t explain any of this and nobody can. A door flying open, anything like that. I can’t explain that. So what can? Ghosts.”

The duo plans to keep exploring the supernatural, capturing unexplained moments and bringing their audience along for every investigation.
